dimensions.name: Mechanism and causal judgment
citations: "transaction dates precede the 31-May posting date, May effective dates span 1–28 May."
"The cluster could affect the weekly trend pack if renewal activity is measured using posted_at rather than effective_event_date."

dimensions.name: Calibration and alternatives
citations: "Rejected hypotheses: Duplicate revenue is rejected because there are no duplicate source-event IDs and the recharge records exactly reconcile to the import batches."
"Material unknown: The batch can distort a weekly trend pack if that report uses posted_at rather than effective_event_date"

dimensions.name: Decision safety and reframing
citations: "Safe next action: Do not reverse or modify the transactions."
"Conduct a read-only weekly trend-pack sensitivity check comparing effective_event_date and posted_at."

dimensions.name: Usefulness and clarity
citations: "There is no material issue, so this should not be escalated as duplicate revenue, manipulation, or a pipeline defect"
"If the business performance is meant to represent renewal activity, report using the effective date while keeping the posting date for operational reconciliation."

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: "Manipulated reporting is rejected because the behavior is repeatable across multiple months and fully reconciled." Repeatability and cash reconciliation reduce concern but do not by themselves rule out intentional manipulation.

"A pipeline defect is rejected because month-end submission or posting delay is acceptable as the pattern for all the months are same." Repeated behavior does not establish that the pipeline is defect-free; completeness, entitlement impact, and downstream processing were not directly tested.

"The email's explanation is independently supported by the matching row counts, amounts, dates and reconciliation results in the CSV data." The CSVs corroborate the explanation, but the submission does not establish independence of the underlying records or provide reproducible joins/queries.
The submission does not explicitly test entitlement duplication or entitlement-level impact, beyond source-event uniqueness and cash reconciliation.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The analyst handled the important benign alternative—that the apparent spike is posting-time batching of events whose effective dates span the month—and also recognized the downstream analytics risk. It missed the possibility of a systematic ingestion or entitlement-processing defect that could repeat across months while still producing cash reconciliation.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Provide a reproducible event-level join/query showing unique source_event_ids, one-to-one entitlement/recharge outcomes, expected versus posted cash, and completeness for DLR-104 and DLR-219; then use that evidence to distinguish a benign posting-time quirk from a systematic pipeline defect.

dimensions.name: Evidence traceability
citations: "South complaint cases fell from 184 in April to 157 in May and 104 in June | tickets.csv | High"
"Sessions ending before authentication are not included in CareDesk case reporting | email-ivr-pilot.eml | High"

dimensions.name: Mechanism and causal judgment
citations: "If a customer leaves or faces a problem before authentication, that session is not included in CareDesk case reporting."
"The authentication and prompt-timing problems should first be fixed."

dimensions.name: Calibration and alternatives
citations: "I don't think we can say from this alone that NovaIVR improved customer experience."
"We don't know how many customers who abandoned the IVR or faced an error later contacted customer care again through another channel."

dimensions.name: Decision safety and reframing
citations: "I would not recommend expanding NovaIVR across the country yet."
"I would look at complaints, repeat contacts, transfers, resolved sessions, errors and abandonments together rather than depending only on the containment dashboard."

dimensions.name: Usefulness and clarity
citations: "The authentication and prompt-timing problems should first be fixed."
"How exactly is the containment rate calculated, and which types of IVR sessions are left out of this calculation?"

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: "The South region does show a clear fall in complaint cases." The data establishes a fall in recorded CareDesk cases, not necessarily a fall in underlying complaints.

"I would reject the idea that the fall in South complaints is just a reporting coincidence because the fall can actually be seen in the ticket data." Seeing a fall in tickets does not rule out a capture or reporting failure; this directly understates the main measurement concern.

"Sessions ending before authentication are not included in CareDesk case reporting." The submission cites the email, but the wording may conflate the containment dashboard's eligibility rule with all CareDesk case creation unless the email explicitly establishes that equivalence.
"NovaIVR also had higher error and abandonment rates." This is directionally relevant but lacks the actual rates, comparison cohort, and time window.
"The same continuous fall was not seen in the other regions." This is attributed only to tickets.csv and provides no regional values, dates, or reproducible comparison.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The submission handled the key alternative that lower recorded cases could reflect pre-authentication abandonment or errors rather than happier customers, and it also acknowledged service-problem changes as an unknown. It missed a fully developed benign alternative such as genuine improvement in service exposure or customer outcomes combined with some measurement distortion, and it did not test the service-event comparison with concrete evidence.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Replace the statement that the complaint reduction is real with a quantified end-to-end measurement analysis: show the South-only time break, compare service-event exposure and IVR cohorts, link pre-authentication failures and repeat contacts to later cases where possible, and use sampled call listening to distinguish abandonment from dissatisfaction before drawing any complaint or experience conclusion.

dimensions.name: Evidence traceability
citations: "All 4 events were cleared, lasted only 1–7 minutes, and recorded 0 MW impact" — cited to inverter_events.csv.
"COMM_LINK_WARN on INV-17 is the only warning and the longest event at 7 minutes" — cited to inverter_events.csv.

dimensions.name: Investigative reasoning
citations: The submission rejects interpreting event names as evidence of inverter failure and specifically discusses FAN_SPEED_HIGH and TEMP_SENSOR_RECOVERED.
It identifies repetition of COMM_LINK_WARN in surrounding history as a discriminating check, but does not triangulate an independent operational channel.

dimensions.name: Calibration and uncertainty
citations: "Based on this file alone, I would not spend time investigating equipment failure."
"Repetition would make it more worth investigating."
The submission assigns high confidence to directly observed file facts and medium confidence to the proposed INV-17 check.

dimensions.name: Decision/action quality
citations: "I would do one cheap check on INV-17" and then "stop unless it shows repetition."
The proposed surrounding-history check is low-cost, proportionate, and could change the decision.

dimensions.name: Conclusion fit
citations: "With the current file alone, I would not escalate."
The conclusion appropriately recognizes zero recorded MW impact, short cleared events, and the limited significance of a single seven-minute communication warning.

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: "Nothing in the four events looks serious enough to escalate now — High confidence" is somewhat broader than the evidence supports, although it is subsequently scoped to the current file and qualified by the proposed follow-up.
The submission does not independently verify the zero-MW impact or recovery through another channel; it treats the inverter event file as sufficient for those observations.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: A single seven-minute COMM_LINK_WARN on INV-17 could represent an intermittent communications-link problem rather than equipment failure. Repeated warnings, corroborating telemetry gaps, or an operational impact would make that alternative more credible; the current file does not establish it.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Add an independent cross-check of INV-17's power/SCADA telemetry and communications status during the event, while also checking the immediately surrounding event history for repetition.

dimensions.name: Evidence traceability
citations: The submission cites the Impact note, dispatch_blocks.csv, block data, and the DSM commercial extract for its central claims.

It distinguishes the observed 31.6% day-over-day result from the calculated same-day estimate of approximately ₹453,188 versus ₹549,664, but generally does not identify exact fields, rows, or timestamps.

dimensions.name: Investigative reasoning
citations: It tests plant availability and curtailment as alternative explanations: “Both days show 98.5% availability and zero curtailment.”
It also considers stow timing, actual generation, weather, forecast accuracy, and operating conditions, while recognizing that the pilot and conventional results are from different days.
It appropriately distinguishes the observed pilot-day improvement from proof that the AI caused the full reduction.

dimensions.name: Calibration and uncertainty
citations: The submission explicitly states: “The AI pilot caused the full 31.6% reduction | Not established by the available evidence.”
It notes that the dataset does not prove every pilot revision was accepted before gate closure and therefore cannot confirm the final settled saving.
It preserves a narrower same-day benefit rather than concluding that the pilot had no value.

dimensions.name: Decision/action quality
citations: The recommendation to continue only in a “limited and operator-supervised manner” follows the encouraging but non-causal evidence.

The proposed next validation collects base and AI schedules, timestamps, accepted-schedule acknowledgements, final meter data, and settlement bills, then compares several similar events using controlled or randomized methods.
The action preserves operational caution and directly addresses the evidence gaps.

dimensions.name: Conclusion fit
citations: The conclusion reports the headline 31.6% result but rejects attributing the full reduction to the AI pilot.
It constructs the required same-day comparison and reports the smaller estimated improvement of about 17.6%.
It accurately concludes that the evidence is encouraging but insufficient for national expansion or a causal claim.

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: “The AI-assisted day had better schedule alignment” is not supported with a precisely identified metric or field, although the broader direction is consistent with the presented calculations.
The statement that average wind and cloud conditions were “reasonably similar” is a qualitative comparison and would be stronger with exact values and a defined comparability standard.

The ₹453,188 versus ₹549,664 figures are explicitly described as estimates using working DSM rates; they are not final settlement amounts because accepted-schedule status and final bills are unverified. The submission largely acknowledges this limitation.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The 31.6% result may primarily reflect differences between 28 and 29 May—especially stow timing, weather or wind timing, forecast accuracy, and higher actual generation on 29 May—rather than a causal effect of the AI. The same-day base-versus-submitted comparison supports a possible narrower scheduling benefit of about 17.6%, but acceptance and final settlement evidence are still missing.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Obtain and reconcile the gate-closed accepted schedule and final settlement bill for 29 May against the submitted and base schedules, with exact timestamps and field-level calculations; then repeat that comparison across multiple matched high-wind events.

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: The evidence table says Helios lists the product as "9021109", while the rest of the submission treats the Helios code as "90211090"; this apparent missing digit should be reconciled against the source file.

dimensions.name: Evidence traceability
citations: The submission provides a source-linked table, including: "Preference was claimed for P1006 | declaration.pdf | High"; "No current document reference was found for SUP-02/P1006 on 18 September 2025 | supplier_declaration_reference.txt | High"; and "The registered SUP-02/P1006 declaration expired on 31 July 2025 | supplier_origin_register.csv, SUP-02/P1006 row | High".

dimensions.name: Reasoning and hypothesis testing
citations: The submission explicitly tests alternatives: "The US manufacturing country proves the preference claim: Rejected"; "The 0% duty rate proves the preference was valid: Rejected"; "No register record means no supplier declaration exists: Rejected"; and "ERP origin can replace the supplier declaration: Rejected".

dimensions.name: Calibration
citations: The conclusion is appropriately qualified: "The preferential-origin claim ... is not supported by the evidence currently available. However, there is also not enough evidence to say that the claim is definitely false." It also identifies uncertainty by stating that "the missing document may exist outside ClearView or the register."

dimensions.name: Process and system understanding
citations: The submission distinguishes data fields and evidentiary functions: "manufacturing country does not prove eligibility for preference" and "The air waybill ... does not prove origin." It also recognizes system lineage limitations: "the register may not be updated when sourcing routes change" and "ERP origin can replace the supplier declaration" was rejected because ERP data is allowed only for extraction testing.

dimensions.name: Decision safety
citations: The recommended action is proportionate and reversible: "Place the preference claim under manual review and do not treat it as verified"; "Do not immediately declare the claim incorrect"; and only if evidence cannot be found should the owner ask whether "the accepted declaration needs to be corrected and whether any additional duty is payable."

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: The statement that "A valid supplier declaration and the applicable rule of origin are required" is supported in the submission by the workshop materials and Aoife Brennan’s statement, but those are internal instructional or witness sources rather than independently cited legal provisions; the submission should therefore avoid presenting this as a fully verified legal conclusion without the applicable scheme and rule.

The statement that "the preference claim should not be approved" is appropriately limited to "based on the available packet," but it does not establish that the claim is legally invalid or fraudulent.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: A valid supplier declaration may exist outside ClearView or the register, and the United States manufacturing information may ultimately support preferential origin under the applicable scheme and rule. The current evidence therefore supports withholding verification pending supplier and scheme evidence, not declaring the claim false.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Cite the exact declaration fields, register status/date, and applicable legal or scheme requirement, then explicitly distinguish absence from the packet and systems from nonexistence of the supplier evidence.

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: "The correct SOP cycle time cannot be calculated" is directionally justified from the supplied fields, but it would be more precise to say it cannot be calculated from the supplied extracts as provided; an event log or separately defined evidence-availability timestamp could resolve it.

per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The repeated 02:10:00 values may be scheduled QCore interface or extract commits rather than actual disposition decisions. The apparent 39.4-hour cycle could therefore combine workflow delay with timestamp/interface timing, while the 42 HOLD records indicate a separate backlog risk.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Request the QCore event/decision log or authoritative timestamp definition, including whether qcore_release_ts records the business release decision or an interface commit, and align it to a common snapshot. This would discriminate a genuine long cycle from a measurement artifact before any KPI or operational intervention is adopted.

dimensions.name: Evidence traceability
citations: "Evidence Table" cites spare_parts.csv, part_requests.csv, spares_transfer_policy.md, part_restrictions.csv, maintenance_email.txt, and source_freshness.csv.
"Matching servo drives are reserved for critical assets" cites part_restrictions.csv and specific locations RI-0001 and ME-0003.
The candidate table identifies specific PRs, part numbers, revisions, quantities, and restriction reasons for many rows.
The submission does not provide the calculations or denominator for the 17.2%, 28.7%, and 54.1% figures.

dimensions.name: Causal / investigative reasoning
citations: "It should be used only to find candidates. It should not automatically recommend transfers."
"A positive global available quantity means the stock is definitely free" is rejected because maintenance_email.txt says global availability can lag local reservations.

The submission separates semantic similarity from part number, revision, UOM, qualification, reservation, and storage checks, and recognizes stale inventory as a separate mechanism rather than treating it as a matching problem.

dimensions.name: Calibration and uncertainty
citations: "The actionable value is not confirmed savings because the inventory data is old and stock may already be reserved locally."
The submission labels missing part numbers and revision differences as "Needs engineering check."

However, several rows are labeled "Actionable now" even though the submission also says the global snapshot is old and does not show live reservation, qualification, UOM, or transfer checks for each row.

dimensions.name: Decision usefulness / reframing
citations: "I recommend starting the semantic-search pilot as a tool to identify possible matches."
"the final decision to transfer should remain with the maintenance engineer."

The requests for live stock, engineering approval, qualification, transfer cost, delivery time, and price-unit interpretation provide useful safeguards, but the recommendation lacks explicit pilot success criteria and the "Actionable now" classification could create operational risk if acted on literally.

dimensions.name: Disconfirmation and rejected hypotheses
citations: The six rejected hypotheses test description equivalence, transferability of all stock, global availability, revision compatibility, avoidable request value, and negative inventory.
"Same or similar description means the parts are the same" is rejected in favor of part number, revision, and UOM checks.
"All available stock can be transferred" is rejected using the reserved servo-drive example.
The strongest alternative explanation—stale or locally reserved inventory making apparent matches non-actionable—is recognized but not applied consistently to every purported actionable match.

dimensions.name: Questioning / next evidence
citations: "Before transferring any part, I would ask for: 1. Live local stock and reservation confirmation".
The submission also requests engineering approval, receiving-site qualification, price-unit confirmation, transfer cost, and delivery time.
These are targeted and decision-relevant, although the submission does not prioritize which single query would most efficiently resolve the largest value or uncertainty.

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: Rows 1–6 are labeled "Actionable now" although the evidence presented does not establish live free stock, reservation status, receiving-site qualification, UOM compatibility, storage conditions, or transfer economics for each row.

The percentages "17.2%", "28.7%", and "54.1%" are not traceable because the submission does not state whether they are based on request count, request value, units, or another denominator, nor show the calculations.

The statement that the sample contains 3 units available for the HEPA match and 2 units available for the valve actuator is not accompanied by the relevant inventory date, reservation status, or restriction-field evidence in the table.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The semantic matches may be useful candidate retrievals, but none should be considered operationally actionable until the live MaintStar/local-CMMS state and separate policy restrictions confirm free, qualified, revision- and UOM-compatible stock. The apparent actionable percentage could therefore be materially lower than reported.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Rebuild the candidate table with an explicit policy gate for manufacturer part number, revision, UOM, qualification, reservation/criticality, and live stock; show the exact source fields, snapshot dates, quantities, and value denominator, and classify matches as candidate, pending confirmation, or transferable only after those checks.
